scope: Corollary 6.2 (Few short cyclic paths at one layer) of the manuscript “A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison–Kaplansky projection conjecture” (preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Counterexample-to-the-Kadison-Kaplansky-Projection-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 285 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 df6227b615985805), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a layer and a side. A nonempty cyclically reduced oriented label word is the word of at most one based cyclically nonbacktracking closed path with its base on that layer and side. Consequently the number of vertices of Ai, or of Bi, supporting such a closed path of length at most gi is at most ⌊gi⌋ X a=1 (2mℓ)a . For all sufficiently large ℓ, this is a fraction at most 2−0.9Hi of either vertex set, uniformly in i.
